text:
sofia: Heads-up — queue depth for redwood-13b-v2 (us-west-2, GPU pool: g4dn-heavy) has jumped ~4x over the last 18m, tail latency spiking. Seeing a backlog of ~12k requests in the admission queue.
max: Oof. Any single-op customer causing the spike or many small ones?
sofia: It's spread across customers. p95 token latency up to 1.4s. Queue depth per-model: redwood-13b-v2 ~12k, redwood-7b-quant ~2.1k; region us-west-2 is main hot spot.
irene: Which admission policy is active? fairshare or strict-cap?
sofia: Currently fairshare with per-customer weightings + soft burst. Admission logs show throttles kicking in but we're still accumulating.
raj: Can we route non-latency-sensitive requests to redwood-7b-quant fallback? Config wise we have a compatible variant.
max: Good idea. We should also consider reducing batch_size for 13b to lower latency and free GPU slots, even if it increases per-token cost.
kevin: If we drop batch size we'll use more GPU cycles per token — cost hit, but short term helpful. Any autoscale activity?
sofia: Autoscale tried to add 2 instances but provisioning delayed due to AZ capacity. g4dn-heavy pool showing 0 available instances in us-west-2a.
ops-bot: [alert] Capacity shortage: pool=g4dn-heavy region=us-west-2a available=0 requested=2
sofia: Logs snippet from admission controller:
```
WARN admission: queue_len=12432 model=redwood-13b-v2 region=us-west-2 reason=capacity_wait
INFO shard-scheduler: attempted_scale_up pool=g4dn-heavy want=2 status=pending
```
raj: Can we temporarily lower soft burst window for large customers (reduce to 10s) to stop huge bursts landing?
irene: Yeah, set per-customer burst=10s and tighten weight cap to 0.2 for now. That should throttle big clients.
max: Also push a routing override: route requests with prompt tag "background-job" or "low-priority" to 7b-quant. We have a routing rule template: `route-if header.x-priority==low -> redwood-7b-quant`
sofia: I'm going to patch a canary routing rule and tighten fairshare. Will also tag long-running requests in the queue for possible cancellation if older than 90s.
kevin: Who owns the provisioning handoff? I've got a ticket open with cloud procurement for extra capacity but that won't be immediate.
sofia: Assigning oncall: @max to run immediate mitigations (routing + burst caps). @raj to prepare fallback promotions and compatibility checks. @irene to update admission policy. I'll monitor.
max: Doing routing canary now. Command: `rictl route apply --region usw2 --canary-file canary-routes.yaml`
deploy-bot: Deploy started: canary-routes.yaml by max — job 31791
max: Canary live in us-west-2c only. Initial traffic shows 18% of low-priority flows moved to 7b-quant, queue depth in c down 26%.
sofia: Good. We need to expand to the other AZs but stagger to avoid double-provisioning.
raj: Compatibility check: 7b-quant returns slightly shorter completions for the same prompts; ops should update client docs for fallback behavior.
irene: Admission policy change applied: soft_burst_window=10s, per_customer_weight_cap=0.2. Monitoring p95 and queue depth.
ops-bot: [notice] Admission policy updated by irene.
max: Next steps: 1) expand canary to b and a in 5m increments 2) run `rictl capacity request --pool g4dn-heavy --region usw2 --count 2` (still pending) 3) if queue >10k after 20m, enable emergency shedding: drop requests older than 90s.
sofia: Agreed. Also let's run a cost check: if we scale up new machines for 4 hours, estimated incremental cost ~ $7.5k. Is that acceptable?
kevin: Finance OK for emergency spend under $10k in this window. Log spend under ticket INF-4927.
max: Canary expanded to all AZs. Early metrics: overall queue down 45%, p95 latency improving to 0.9s.
sofia: Nice. Keep an eye on model-specific backlog — 13b still high but stabilized at ~6.5k.
raj: I'll open a follow-up to evaluate longer term: pre-warming dedicated spare capacity for peak windows and smarter regional routing to avoid single-region saturation.
sofia: Thanks team. We'll keep monitoring for next 60m, if things hold we'll close this thread. If backlog creeps up again, escalate to infra-planning for capacity commit. :thumbsup:
